title: 'Minor strikes', a task force called Iron Gate, and missiles on Kyiv's Northern Bridge
summary: Trump announces 'minor' US strikes on Iranian air defences as Central Command sets up Task Force Iron Gate against Iran's land routes and offers a reward for nuclear intelligence, Russian missiles hit Kyiv's Northern Bridge ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks, Ukraine strikes the Saratov and Afipsky refineries, and reported strikes in Lebanon and Yemen.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Saturday, November seventh. Yesterday we were talking about a possible US–Iran deal. Today the picture is more mixed.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Right. On Friday, President Trump said the US had carried out what he called minor strikes on Iran's air defences.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: At about the same time, Iranian media reported missiles hitting Qeshm Island, in the Strait of Hormuz. That's the same island the US struck at the start of the week. Trump didn't explicitly say the two were the same thing, though.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And on the diplomatic side, Iran called the latest US reply to its proposal, quote, not convincing. Iran's deputy security chief said they need to see practical measures from the Americans.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So that optimism from yesterday, about Iran opening up on nuclear issues, has cooled a bit.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And then, today, Central Command announced something new. A task force called Iron Gate.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: What does it do?

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: It's meant to disrupt Iran's land routes. So far the US blockade has been at sea, stopping ships going in and out of Iranian ports. Iron Gate targets weapons and banned goods moving over Iran's land borders and across the Caspian Sea.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's small, about twenty people, based at Central Command's headquarters in Tampa. And Admiral Brad Cooper says the sea blockade has already stopped Iran exporting more than twenty-five billion dollars of crude oil.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Central Command also offered a reward of up to twenty million dollars for information about Iran's nuclear programme. Which is interesting, given the administration has said that programme was obliterated.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So, pressure on several fronts, while the talks continue through Qatar.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And at sea, things are a little quieter today, at least in the confirmed reports. But this week saw the Velos Sapphire, where a crew member was killed north of Qatar, and a blast on a tanker off Khasab.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Let's go to Ukraine. Overnight, Russia hit Kyiv hard.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Officials say Russia launched a hundred and seventy-two drones and thirty-six ballistic missiles. In Kyiv, several missiles hit the Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River. It's one of the main crossings in the capital, and it was closed in both directions.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Kyiv's mayor said the strikes damaged the roadway, trolleybus lines and a power line. Energy facilities were also hit. One person was killed and eight were wounded in the Kyiv area, including a child. And another person was killed in the Dnipropetrovsk region.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Russia's defence ministry confirmed the strike. It says the bridge was being used to move weapons and military equipment.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And the timing matters. Russia, Ukraine and the US are due to meet in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. RFE/RL describes it as the fourth round of trilateral talks.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Ukraine's drone campaign against Russian oil kept going too. Overnight, several fires broke out at the Saratov refinery after a drone attack. There's no official damage assessment yet.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And there's more detail on Friday's Afipsky strike, in Krasnodar region. Militarnyi reports one of the refinery's main processing units was damaged. Regional authorities blamed falling drone debris for the fire.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the front line, Ukraine's General Staff reported a hundred and eighty clashes on Friday. And interestingly, attacks around Pokrovsk dropped to just four. That's down from the dozens we saw earlier in the week.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Russian airstrikes continued though. Fifty-three of them, dropping a hundred and seventy guided bombs.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Quick lap of the other fronts. In Yemen, Houthi-affiliated media say the death toll from a Saudi strike in Sanaa province has risen to twenty-two. That figure hasn't been independently verified.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And in southern Lebanon, the Israeli army carried out artillery shelling and a demolition in the village of Bani Haiyyan. No casualties were reported.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the ships, no new reports today. The Theodore Roosevelt was last seen in the South China Sea, heading west. The George Washington and the George H. W. Bush are in the Arabian Sea. And the next USNI fleet tracker is due Monday.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So, what to watch. Whether Trump's minor strikes stay minor, and what Iron Gate actually does in practice. The Abu Dhabi talks on Tuesday, and whether Russia's strike on the bridge affects them. And where the Roosevelt turns up on Monday.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
